overall_reason: A restrained cover card that leads with the product's real menu-bar panel (real process names, real readings) on a deliberate ink-blue theme; the only generic part is the tagline, which says a mood rather than what Mole does.

findings.evidence: "A quiet keeper for your Mac." Failed T-RIVAL-NAME: CleanMyMac, Stats or iStat Menus could all carry it. Failed T-THREE-LINE: not picturable, not falsifiable. 'Quiet' is a virtue word about the product (SLP-135 house voice: warm, modest, literary).
findings.after: Say the job the screenshot proves, e.g. 'CPU, memory, disk and battery in the menu bar; cleans what you uninstall' [DATA NEEDED: Mole's own one-line description]
findings.why: The one line of copy on the card spends itself on tone; T-FIVE-SECOND 'what is it' is answered only by the screenshot.

findings.evidence: The app panel occupies about 350 x 900 px of a 1050 px wide frame; the rest is macOS wallpaper. At feed size (canvas shown ~2.8x smaller) the panel's 11-13 px-equivalent labels (CPU 14%, Top Processes) fall to about 4 px. Failed T-THUMBNAIL for the product evidence.
findings.before: Full wallpaper crop around a narrow panel
findings.after: Crop to the panel (or its top half: score 100, CPU, MEM, Disk) and scale it up so the key readings stay legible in the feed
findings.why: The real product is the card's best material; the wallpaper takes two thirds of its space.

strengths: The image is a real product capture with real process names (Parallels Desktop, Cursor, WeChat), real units and states; nothing is invented or drawn.
One theme, three colours (ink #1B365D, cream text, pale blue accent) chosen as a named variant from a set (paper-ink), not a default gradient.
Hierarchy is clear: maker, name, line, product; no badges, icons, emoji or chrome.
Meta line 'Tw93 Open Source Family' passes T-EYEBROW: it carries attribution and is set in sentence case, not tracked caps.
not_investigated: Charter is not installed in the capture environment; the type rendered as Liberation Serif (fonts.json), so the face itself was not judged
other cards in the set: only the cover was captured
